title: Sanborn-conditioned n-gram prior on the k=4 degeneracy census
hypothesis: an author-specific (K1-K3) n-gram prior tightens the k=4 census toward a unique decryption
best_partial: Sanborn re-rank separation 4.88 sigma; Sanborn-census distinct 0 (vs hexagram 10); prior-robust=True
insights: Built a deterministic char n-gram LM from Sanborn's ACTUAL K1-K3 plaintexts (768 chars, order-4 backoff). CAVEAT: ~768 chars is severely data-starved for a char-LM -- it is spiky and overfits coincidental n-grams, so apparent 'signal' from it is unreliable (the only Sanborn plaintext available is K1-K3; no larger author corpus exists under decipherment-only).

(1) RE-RANK: re-scored the 4 generic-hexagram k=4 census decryptions with the Sanborn-LM; top-vs-rest separation = 4.88 sigma over only 4 candidates. With so few points and a 768-char LM this sigma is NOT statistically meaningful -> treated as no reliable signal.

(2) SANBORN-DRIVEN CENSUS: maximising the Sanborn-LM yields 0 distinct decryptions above its own 5th-pct bar (generic hexagram gave 10 at k=4). san_distinct=0: the bar is UNREACHABLE (the spiky tiny-corpus LM bar is an artifact, not determination) -- not evidence of reduced degeneracy.

VERDICT: the Sanborn-conditioned prior is DATA-LIMITED and does not resolve k=4: the best author-specific n-gram prior buildable from the only available Sanborn text (K1-K3, 768 chars) is too starved to single out the plaintext or to be trusted. The under-determination is PRIOR-ROBUST to the realisable author prior. Consistent with 092/093/107.
next_steps: under-determination is prior-robust to an author-specific n-gram prior. Within decipherment-only and no-LLM, the data does not single out the plaintext.
